suspicions.claim: Looking up a user by username no longer works; the endpoint only searches by email.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with username 'alice' and email 'alice@example.com'. Authenticate and request GET /api/users/alice. Observe 404 instead of the user object.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/alice returned 200 in base and 404 in head across multiple probes, showing username lookup no longer works.

suspicions.claim: If a username equals another user's email, the endpoint returns the wrong user.
suspicions.trigger: Create user A (username='alice', email='alice@example.com') and user B (username='bob', email='bob@example.com'). Request GET /api/users/bob@example.com. Observe user B is returned. Then request GET /api/users/alice (which is not an email). Observe 404. Then create user C with username='bob@example.com'. Request GET /api/users/bob@example.com. Observe user C is returned instead of user B.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/bob@example.com returned 404 in base and 200 in head (returning user B), GET /api/users/alice returned 200 in base and 404 in head, and after creating user C with username bob@example.com the same email request returned user C in base but still user B in head, confirming the endpoint matches email first and returns the wrong user when username equals another's email.

suspicions.claim: The route parameter is still named 'username' in the OpenAPI documentation, misleading clients.
suspicions.trigger: Fetch the API documentation at /docs (or the OpenAPI spec). Inspect the path parameter for GET /api/users/{username}. Observe it is still described as a username, not an email or username.
suspicions.evidence: The probe for s3 fetched /docs and received 200 in both base and head, but the response bodies show only a title and empty arrays with no path parameter details, so the OpenAPI parameter description was not inspected.

suspicions.claim: Usernames that contain '@' (valid per schema) can no longer be looked up because they are treated as emails.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with username 'user@domain' and email 'user@domain@example.com'. Authenticate and request GET /api/users/user@domain. Observe 404 because the code filters by email='user@domain' which does not match.
suspicions.evidence: The probe for s4 failed to create the user (POST /api/users returned 400 in both base and head) and the subsequent GET /api/users/user@domain returned 401 in both, so the triggering input never reached the route.

suspicions.claim: Emails are case-insensitive per RFC, but the filter uses exact match; lookups may fail for differing case.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with email 'Alice@Example.com'. Request GET /api/users/alice@example.com (lowercase). Observe 404 because filter_by(email=...) does exact match.
suspicions.evidence: The probe for s5 created a user with email Alice@Example.com and requested GET /api/users/alice@example.com; base returned 404 while head returned 200 with the user object, showing the head performs a case-insensitive match rather than an exact match.
